secondary.comment: ADR-0059 — was .400. Ladder shifted one step lighter so the tier below it can clear AA

muted.comment: ADR-0059 — was .500 (#757470), which failed AA on ALL THREE dark surfaces: 4.00 on base, 3.48 on raised, 4.49 on sunken. .400 measures 6.88 / 5.99 / 7.72

disabled.comment: ADR-0059 — was .700; kept one step below muted. Deliberately under 4.5:1 per WCAG 1.4.3's inactive-component exemption

on-brand.comment: ADR-0059 — filled brand/semantic grounds carry their own colour in both themes, so the text on them does not invert

link.comment: Lighter step for AA contrast on dark surface

section.comment: ADR-0059 — full-bleed identity grounds. Guide §6.1 presents white, red, green and black as the four official backgrounds; §3.34.1 previously forbade the middle two. Green and red are identical across themes because their hue carries them against either page ground; black is the one register that changes, because pure black on a near-black page measures 1.12:1 and stops being a departure at all.

surface.comment: Not green.500: the identity value stays the brand mark's reference per Chapter 1 ("use the official values literally as the 500 reference"), while a ground carrying two tiers of text needs the step Chapter 1 itself names for higher contrast. white measures 4.81 on .500 versus 9.40 on .700

border.comment: 3.29:1 — clears WCAG 1.4.11 for a control boundary inside the section

divider.comment: 1.95:1 — a decorative rule, never a control boundary

surface.comment: white measures 5.88 on red.500 versus 8.14 on .600

border.comment: 8.14:1. No step of the red ramp reaches 3:1 against red.600 without turning pink, so the control boundary here is white — which is also what the guide's own red materials use (white strokes on the referee kit §2.3 and every local-championship garment)

surface.comment: ADR-0059 — the one register that differs by theme. Pure black against this theme's #131210 page measures 1.12:1, i.e. no section boundary at all. neutral-warm.700 measures 2.07 against the page while keeping both text tiers over AA (9.04 and 4.75). Rejected neutral-warm.800: better muted contrast (6.75) but only 1.46 separation, which is not a section

border.comment: 6.78:1. Was neutral-warm.300, which measures 4.75:1 — passing, but identical to text-muted, so a control boundary and a body-text tier rendered as the same colour

divider.comment: 1.93:1 — decorative rule only. Was neutral-warm.600 at 1.43:1, below the point a rule is reliably perceptible

adjacent-separator.comment: ADR-0059 — MANDATORY between a green and a red section. Measured contrast between the two registers is 1.15:1: stacked directly they have no visible boundary whatsoever, and the pair is the classic red/green confusion besides. The guide never abuts them either — in the four-stroke motif there is always white or black between

subtle.comment: ADR-0059 — deliberately EQUAL to border.default in this theme, not a distinct value. The neutral ramp has no step between .800 (the default rule) and .900 (which is surface.raised itself), so a genuinely fainter rule would be invisible against the card it divides. Light theme does have the .150 step and so does differentiate

strong.comment: ADR-0051 — corrected from neutral-warm.600 (2.97:1 on neutral-warm.950, fails); .500 measures 4.00:1

card.comment: ADR-0052 — dark-mode shadows need much higher opacity than light-mode (0.06) to register against an already-dark surface; the surface adapts, brand colors don't invert (Brand Guide v1.0 §11.1 principle applied to elevation)
